opening.text: Road signs can feel like rules. Slow down. Stop. Curve ahead. But nobody puts up a sign to spoil your trip. Someone who knew the road put it there to keep you safe. God's commandments are signs like that. They come from One who knows the whole road and loves the traveler.

mainMessage.text: God gives commandments out of love. When we keep them, we find happiness, knowledge and peace.

blocks.text: **Signs from someone who cares** The Lord gave His people commands for their good. They are not meant to trap us.
And the Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as it is at this day.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Keep the Commandments” from the October 2015 general conference.
God’s commandments are not given to frustrate us or to become obstacles to our happiness.
They are given for our good.
**Why we follow the signs** We don't obey out of fear. We obey out of love.
If ye love me, keep my commandments.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “If Ye Love Me, Keep My Commandments” from the April 2014 general conference.
Our love of the Savior is the key to Savior-like obedience.
Love is the reason.
**Learning the road by driving it** We understand a road by traveling it. Truth becomes clear when we live it.
If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Obedience Brings Blessings” from the April 2013 general conference.
A knowledge of truth and the answers to our greatest questions come to us as we are obedient to the commandments of God.
Obey, and we will know.
**When we miss a turn** Everyone misses a turn. The Lord doesn't leave us lost. We can turn around and begin again.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “If Ye Love Me, Keep My Commandments” from the April 2014 general conference.
As we repent by turning away from disobedience and by beginning to obey again, we show our love for Him.
Turn around and begin again.
**Others have driven it before** Prophets have walked this road. They found strength and knowledge on it.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Obedience Brings Blessings” from the April 2013 general conference.
Obedience is a hallmark of prophets; it has provided strength and knowledge to them throughout the ages.
Prophets show the way.
**The road leads to joy** The road has a destination. It is a place of lasting happiness.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Keep the Commandments” from the October 2015 general conference.
May we realize that our greatest happiness in this life will come as we follow God’s commandments and obey His laws!
The road leads to joy.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when keeping a commandment brought a blessing they did not expect. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Noah obeys

blocks.text: God told Noah to build an ark. There was no rain yet. People around him didn't understand.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he. And Noah did according unto all that the Lord commanded him.
Noah obeyed before he could see why. He trusted the One who gave the sign. When the flood came, he was ready.

application.text: First, pick one commandment you want to keep better. Second, ask yourself why God gave it. Third, keep it for one week and note what changes.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God gives commandments because He loves us. I know obedience brings peace. I know Jesus Christ kept every commandment perfectly. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to pick one commandment you want to keep better.
I invite you to ask yourself why God gave it.
I invite you to keep it for one week and note what changes.
blessings: You will understand His purpose more clearly.

closingVerse.text:
If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments, and abide in his love.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.

opening.text: A climbing vine will sprawl on the ground if left alone. Give it a trellis, and it climbs. It grows taller and bears more fruit. The trellis doesn't hurt the vine. It helps the vine become what it was meant to be. Commandments are a trellis for our lives.

mainMessage.text: The commandments are a trellis. They help us grow upward toward God.

blocks.text: **Support, not a cage** A trellis holds the vine up. God's commandments hold us up.
And the Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as it is at this day.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Keep the Commandments” from the October 2015 general conference.
God’s commandments are not given to frustrate us or to become obstacles to our happiness.
They lift us up.

If ye love me, keep my commandments.

Our love of the Savior is the key to Savior-like obedience.
Love draws us up.

If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Obedience Brings Blessings” from the April 2013 general conference.
A knowledge of truth and the answers to our greatest questions come to us as we are obedient to the commandments of God.
The view grows wider.
**When the vine slips** Sometimes a vine slips off the trellis. The gardener lifts it and ties it back. The Lord does this for us when we repent.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “If Ye Love Me, Keep My Commandments” from the April 2014 general conference.
As we repent by turning away from disobedience and by beginning to obey again, we show our love for Him.
He ties us back.
**Vines that grew before us** Prophets climbed this trellis before us. Their strength and knowledge came from obeying.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Obedience Brings Blessings” from the April 2013 general conference.
Obedience is a hallmark of prophets; it has provided strength and knowledge to them throughout the ages.
Prophets climbed it first.
**The fruit** A vine on a trellis bears fruit. A life of obedience bears happiness and peace.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Keep the Commandments” from the October 2015 general conference.
May we realize that our greatest happiness in this life will come as we follow God’s commandments and obey His laws!
The fruit is joy.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they followed a plain instruction and were glad they did. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Adam obeys

blocks.text: Adam and Eve were sent out into a hard world. God gave them commandments to follow.

And he gave unto them commandments, that they should worship the Lord their God, and should offer the firstlings of their flocks, for an offering unto the Lord. And Adam was obedient unto the commandments of the Lord.
Adam didn't ask for every reason first. He was obedient, and God spoke to him through an angel after many days. Obedience opened the door to learning more.

application.text: First, find one place where you feel stuck or flat. Second, ask what commandment could support you there. Third, begin it today.

Start a fresh batch.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they followed a simple instruction and it worked. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Naaman washes

blocks.text: Naaman was a great captain with leprosy. The prophet Elisha told him to wash in the Jordan seven times. Naaman was angry at first. The instruction seemed too simple.

And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean. Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.
The steps looked small. But Naaman followed them, and he was healed. Simple things, done in faith, can change a life.

application.text: First, choose one “step” you have been skipping. Second, do it every day for a week. Third, write down what you notice.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the commandments are simple and they work. I know God keeps His promises. I know Jesus Christ is the Bread of Life. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to choose one step you have been skipping.
I invite you to do it every day for a week.
I invite you to write down what you notice.
blessings: You will see the blessings of obedience.
You will feel the Spirit more.

closingVerse.text:
There is a law, irrevocably decreed in heaven before the foundations of this world, upon which all blessings are predicated—
And when we obtain any blessing from God, it is by obedience to that law upon which it is predicated.

opening.text: Before every flight, a pilot goes through a checklist. Even the most experienced pilots do it. They don't skip steps because they feel sure. A missed step can cost lives. The checklist isn't an insult to the pilot. It is how pilots stay safe. God's commandments are a checklist for the flight of life.

mainMessage.text: The commandments are a checklist given by the One who built the plane. Following them keeps us safe and gets us home.

blocks.text: **Written to protect** The checklist wasn't written to slow the pilot. It was written to bring everyone home safely.
And the Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as it is at this day.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Keep the Commandments” from the October 2015 general conference.
God’s commandments are not given to frustrate us or to become obstacles to our happiness.
They protect us.
**Flying for the ones we love** A pilot checks everything because of the people on board. We keep God's commandments because of the One we love.
If ye love me, keep my commandments.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “If Ye Love Me, Keep My Commandments” from the April 2014 general conference.
Our love of the Savior is the key to Savior-like obedience.
Love is why we check.
**Clear skies, clear answers** When the pilot follows each step, the flight is smooth. When we obey, answers come more clearly.
If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Obedience Brings Blessings” from the April 2013 general conference.
A knowledge of truth and the answers to our greatest questions come to us as we are obedient to the commandments of God.
The skies clear.
**When a step is missed** Pilots who find a missed step go back and fix it. They don't pretend. We can do the same with repentance.
I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.
Elder Robert D. Hales of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “If Ye Love Me, Keep My Commandments” from the April 2014 general conference.
As we repent by turning away from disobedience and by beginning to obey again, we show our love for Him.
Go back and fix it.
**Flown by those before us** Others have flown this route. Prophets trusted the checklist, and it brought them strength and knowledge.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.
President Thomas S. Monson, President of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, said this in his talk “Obedience Brings Blessings” from the April 2013 general conference.

**Landing safely** The flight ends at home. The Lord promised a happy state to those who keep His commandments.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. May we realize that our greatest happiness in this life will come as we follow God’s commandments and obey His laws!
Home at last.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they chose to obey fully, not just partly. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Saul keeps back part

blocks.text: God told King Saul to do a certain thing completely. Saul did most of it and kept some for himself. Samuel confronted him.
And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
Saul thought partial obedience was enough. Samuel taught that God wants a willing heart and full obedience, not a good-looking offering.

application.text: First, ask whether any commandment is one you keep “mostly.” Second, choose to keep that one fully this week. Third, tell God what you are doing.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God asks for our whole heart. I know His way is safe. I know Jesus Christ is the Captain of our salvation. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to ask whether any commandment is one you keep "mostly."
I invite you to choose to keep that one fully this week.
I invite you to tell God what you are doing.

closingVerse.text: And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great a delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.

opening.text: When a toddler is learning to walk the stairs, a parent puts up a gate and holds the handrail. The child may not like it. But the parent isn't trying to limit the child. The parent is trying to keep the child safe until the child can climb alone. God is a loving Parent. His commandments are the handrail on the stairs.

mainMessage.text: God's commandments are the handrail of a loving Parent. They keep us steady while we climb.

blocks.text: **A Parent's care** The handrail is there because someone cares. God gave His commands for our good.

He sets us on our feet.
**Learning from those who climbed** Prophets climbed the same stairs. They held on, and they grew strong and wise.

**The top of the stairs** The stairs lead somewhere good. The Lord promised His faithful children happiness that has no end.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they learned obedience through something hard. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus Christ learned obedience

blocks.text: The Savior Himself walked this road. Paul wrote about it.
Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;
Jesus Christ was the perfect Son. He still learned obedience through hard things. If He walked the stairs one step at a time, we can too, and He walks with us.

application.text: First, think of one commandment that feels like a handrail and not a limit. Second, thank God for it. Third, help someone else who is learning to climb.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God is a loving Parent. I know His commandments keep me steady. I know Jesus Christ kept every commandment so He could lift me. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of one commandment that feels like a handrail and not a limit, and thank God for it.
I invite you to help someone else who is learning to climb.
I invite you to thank God in prayer for His guidance.
blessings: You will feel gratitude for His laws.
You will see His love in His commandments.

closingVerse.text: Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;
